title: Basis of the Service Charge on the Overdue Balance of a Crop Input Purchasing Account
content:
**1.** The service charge a crop input account carries is worked out on the overdue balance of the account as a whole rather than invoice by invoice, and one charge is booked for the statement month then running against the oldest invoice on the account that has run past the programme's terms and still stands unpaid.

**2. The overdue balance.** The overdue balance is everything invoiced to the account that has run past the programme's terms, which is every delivery invoiced to it apart from those invoiced within the statement months the programme's terms cover, the programme's terms in days being taken over a statement month of 30 days. That balance is reduced by every payment posted to the account, by every credit memo written on it and by every discount granted on it, whatever the invoice each was written against, and is increased by every service charge already standing on it.

**3. The rate.** The monthly service rate is the rate the programme carries.

**4. The days.** The overdue days are counted from the date the account went past due, that date counting as day zero, to the handling date on which the charge is worked out. The days of grace allowed before the charge bites are the grace days the programme carries. The chargeable days are the overdue days less the days of grace, and where that difference is negative the chargeable days are nil.

**5. The balance the rate acts on.** The share of the discounts granted on the account that is added back before the charge is worked out is nil. The balance the rate acts on is the overdue balance plus the share added back of the discounts granted on the account, rounded half away from zero to two decimal places.

**6. The charge at the rate.** The charge at the rate is that balance multiplied by the monthly service rate and then multiplied by the chargeable days over a statement month of 30 days, rounded half away from zero to two decimal places once at the end of that step. The charge stands as worked out at the rate.

**7. The charge booked.** The collection handling sum added to the charge is nil. The service charge booked is the charge after relief plus the collection handling sum, and where that total falls under the programme's service charge floor the floor is booked instead; the result is rounded half away from zero to two decimal places once at the end.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A member on a programme of the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts carrying terms of 180 calendar days, a monthly service rate of 1.25 percent, 15 days of grace and a floor of 10.00 USD. Terms of 180 days taken over a statement month of 30 days cover 6 statement months.

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Everything invoiced to the account | 96000.00 USD |
| Invoiced within the 6 statement months the terms cover | 54000.00 USD |
| Invoiced and run past the terms | 42000.00 USD |
| Less payments posted | 12000.00 USD |
| Less credit memos written | 1500.00 USD |
| Less discounts granted | 800.00 USD |
| Plus service charges already standing | 300.00 USD |
| Overdue balance | 28000.00 USD |
| Share of the discounts added back | nil |
| Balance the rate acts on | 28000.00 USD |
| Overdue days, the past-due date being day zero | 52 |
| Days of grace | 15 |
| Chargeable days | 37 |
| Charge at the rate | 431.67 USD |
| Collection handling sum | nil |
| Total against the floor of 10.00 USD | 431.67 USD |
| Service charge booked | 431.67 USD |

Had the chargeable days come out negative they would be nil, the charge at the rate would be nil, and the floor of 10.00 USD would be what is booked.
